creator: Alexander Terp
description:
#153 Tier 1. ``x = $`cmd` `` binds `0` rather than the output, and stringifies happily downstream. The most natural-looking capture is the wrong one, and nothing errors.

#153 proposes the cheap defusal: a lint on a single non-`code` variable later used as a string. Whether the capture semantics themselves should change is a larger question - the lint stands on its own.

---

### Orientation

- `core/` owns the runtime semantics; `rts/check/` owns the lint. `rts` must not import `core`.
- The capture-arity rule is `core/shell.go:97` `positionalCaptureMode`: `captureStdout = numVars >= 2`, `captureStderr = numVars >= 3`. One target means nothing is captured, so `core/shell.go:351` `assignShellResults` puts the exit code on target 0.
- The named form already works and is the fix to point users at: `core/shell.go:103` `namedCaptureMode` recognizes targets literally named `code`, `stdout`, `stderr`.
- The checker already binds shell targets - `rts/check/binder.go:445` `visitShell` calls `declareTarget` on each - but never types them. `*rl.Shell` appears in `rts/check/type_check.go` only at `:321` (`markGuarded`) and `:1169` (`collectAssignedSymsIn`); `walkStmt` at `rts/check/type_check.go:764` has no `Shell` case. So today the checker does not know `x` is an int.

### Watch out for

- This card is scoped to a lint, not a semantics change. If the capture semantics themselves get revisited later, that is a breaking change with the three-layer migration obligation from AGENTS.md (migration diagnostic, error doc, `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.X.md` entry) and a `fix!:` prefix.
- `core/error_docs/` has its own style guide at `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`.
- `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/` are generated from `core/error_docs/`. Edit the source and run `make generate`.
title: Defuse single-variable shell capture binding the exit code
